## Demo and approval

Two visibly distinct people provide stronger evidence of a shared workflow and make the handoff easier to follow. This is a plausible presentation advantage, not an automatic score increase: Switch centrality is 30% and Presentation 20%, with reproducibility also judged. Keep synthetic lab records clearly labeled; replace the builder-plays-both disclaimer with “Synthetic lab data; two real teammates playing student and PI,” and show each person's actual display name and role. Disclose edits and elapsed waits. [docs/flip-the-switch-hackathon.md:106-118; docs/plan/04-demo.md:9-14, 30-32]

**Target 2:15, under 3:00:** 0:00-0:15 establish problem, two names and shared room; 0:15-0:40 student requests 60 minutes and `@labops` names conflict; 0:40-1:05 show 15:45-16:45 alternative and the request ID; 1:05-1:30 student attempts a decision and is refused, then PI sees the same full request and chooses Allow once; 1:30-1:50 show the matching committed booking and audit reference; 1:50-2:05 actual Wispr evidence if available; 2:05-2:15 show README and reproducibility. Hold important card fields legibly and caption actual wait time. This requires the installed-runtime gate and student refusal to pass; otherwise cut the decision and commit shots, show proposal and “unapproved; booking status unverified,” and only claim no booking for that request if the scoped ledger query proves it. [docs/plan/04-demo.md:28, 49, 53-57; docs/build/PHASES.md:50-52]

**One eligible approver remains correct.** Two humans do not create a quorum requirement. The PI can be the teammate only if the approver agent is owned by the teammate's distinct Switch user, that person's chat account is linked, agents are reconfigured as needed, and the entire actual configuration passes all permission and card tests. A teammate on a separate machine does not become owner by joining Mattermost. `owner_agents` means agents owned by the same person; the policy also admits the owner human, not arbitrary teammates. With Nikhil owning `@pi-desk`, the teammate cannot answer its owner-scoped card merely by being a member. An intentional policy expansion would require a newly designed and recertified authorization boundary and is not recommended. [switch/docs/official/internals/identity-and-access.md:98-130; docs/plan/02-product.md:30-36; docs/plan/03-architecture.md:86-105]

The pinned `bridge_answers.py` says both button and typed answers reach the approval service; it identifies the actor, refuses absent identity, and passes the identified person to the approval check. Addressing policy is therefore relevant to answers, but a correct source-level reading is not a runtime pass. Claim both distinct platform identities where possible; prove the student rejection, owner acceptance, repeated fresh cards and zero unauthorized commits. If the local server prevents the teammate from independently claiming a Switch identity, their student message may still reach an open-policy helper, but a claimed-student refusal test remains **UNVERIFIED** until actually arranged and observed. [switch/core/switch_core/session_activity/bridge_answers.py:1-9, 88-126, 128-153, 177-205; switch/docs/official/internals/identity-and-access.md:124-134; docs/build/PHASES.md:50-52]

## Joining the real room: choices

All paths need distinct Mattermost or hosted-chat accounts, room membership, a working agent, and a fresh acceptance test of the chosen chat and identity combination. Linking a messaging identity to a Switch user is separate from joining chat; the platform account must be visible to the bridge, and each person normally links themselves in Console. The local Switch server itself is documented as unavailable to colleagues, so remote Console access and independent claims cannot be assumed. [switch/docs/official/getting-started/add-a-server.md:25-45, 72-100; switch/docs/official/deploy/messaging-apps/how-connections-work.md:73-79]

1. **Same LAN, Mattermost; primary when co-located (30-60 min estimate).** Check the actual Docker published host port and interface, Mattermost listen address and Windows firewall; ensure the teammate can reach only the needed host and port on a trusted private network. Configure Mattermost `SiteURL` for the reachable address if necessary, preserving the bridge's working access; invite/create a distinct user and join the existing team/channel. Verify login, bidirectional messages, WebSocket updates, agent response and card/refusal before filming. `localhost` bind, guest Wi-Fi isolation, firewall rules, a changed SiteURL breaking the bridge, or no TLS can fail it; no public port forwarding. Exact Console-managed binding and whether a SiteURL change survives restart are **UNVERIFIED**. [Mattermost architecture](https://docs.mattermost.com/deployment-guide/application-architecture); [Mattermost configuration](https://docs.mattermost.com/administration-guide/configure/environment-variables); [switch/docs/official/getting-started/add-a-server.md:35-45]
2. **Discord bridge; primary when remote, fallback when LAN fails (45-90 min estimate).** Create a private server/channel with two real Discord users; configure a Discord bot, required intents and permissions including webhooks, connect it in Switch Console as server admin, link the PI account, post an ordinary message to instantiate the room, invite agents, and rerun the full certification for that bridge. Risks: bot permissions, account linking, new room/template setup, differing card behavior and bot token leakage. The bridge reaches hosted chat while Switch remains on Nikhil's machine; it does not make the local Switch server itself accessible to another Console. Student independent claim remains a separate unresolved prerequisite. [switch/docs/official/deploy/messaging-apps/discord.md:7-13, 22-28, 35-46, 76-101; switch/docs/official/deploy/messaging-apps/how-connections-work.md:15-31, 73-79]
3. **Private tunnel to Mattermost (60-120 min estimate).** Tailscale: install on both machines, authorize only the teammate/device, reach the host's private address and published Mattermost port, scope firewall, and check SiteURL and WebSockets. Cloudflare Tunnel: connect the Mattermost origin through an authenticated, access-restricted hostname and verify browser sessions and WebSockets. Account, domain, policy, HTTPS and exact configuration requirements are **UNVERIFIED** here. Risks include accidental broad exposure, split URLs breaking the bridge, authentication policy interference and real-time disconnects. A tunnel does not by itself create a Switch user or certify approvals. [Mattermost architecture](https://docs.mattermost.com/deployment-guide/application-architecture); [switch/docs/official/internals/identity-and-access.md:124-134]
4. **Remote Switch host (2-4+ hours estimate; last resort).** Provision an SSH-accessible Linux/macOS host with Docker, working SSH key and sudo; onboard it in Console and deploy a server; separately solve reachable Gateway/API and chat hosting, re-onboard agents and rerun gates. The documented remote-host setup is not automatically an address to hand to colleagues; Windows is not a supported remote host, and reboot needs manual restart. Migration, credential exposure, downtime and recertification consume the deadline. [switch/docs/official/deploy/host-remotely.md:7-27, 50-58, 70-82; switch/docs/official/getting-started/add-a-server.md:51-64]

## Scope and risks

Extra human capacity buys testing, evidence and presentation first, not a free feature. After P4 is independently green and filming/submission protected, P5 ranks separately built and gated stale detection first, citation verification second, inventory holds third. Stale is newly more affordable only if an actual coding, testing and audit timebox remains; no added people automatically supply that capacity. Cite only a proven stale result; no blocked release or renewed approval claim without the complete certified loop. Literature metadata is not claim support; inventory is background until built. No change to booking invariants, single-approver authorization, fresh-card requirements, failure-closed fallback, test-first discipline or gates. [docs/build/PHASES.md:50-56; docs/plan/02-product.md:93-121; docs/plan/08-build-schedule.md:24-28, 73-83]

New risks: mistaken ownership or identity claims (test distinct users and zero unauthorized commits); network exposure or credential leaks (private room, restricted access and secret review); bridge change invalidating earlier tests (pin tuple and rerun certification); mismatched calendars or teammate availability (prebook rehearsal and retain baseline); cross-branch collisions (single integrator, narrow ownership); late edits and competing publication (freeze and 19:00 target); overclaiming synthetic roles, cards or voice usage (show actual evidence only). Local-server accessibility, per-user claims, branch protection and all setup durations remain **UNVERIFIED**. [switch/docs/official/internals/identity-and-access.md:98-134; docs/plan/03-architecture.md:90-105; docs/plan/09-submission-and-risks.md:75-89]

## Orchestrator decisions (Thu 5 Nov 2026, 13:50 IST)

The teammate is remote (confirmed by Nikhil). Decisions taken from the analysis above:

1. **Roles.** Nikhil stays the Switch agent owner and the PI approver of `@pi-desk`. The teammate is the student and requester, using their own chat account and real display name with a "(student role, synthetic lab data)" label. Approval stays single-approver and owner-scoped; it is not widened.
2. **One chat platform for automation and demo: Mattermost.** The Playwright two-persona harness needs local persona accounts, and automating a personal Discord account is not an option. The teammate reaches the same Mattermost through a private Tailscale share (primary). The fallback is a private Discord bridge used only for the human demo, with its own certification run. Public port forwarding is not allowed.
3. **Teammate ownership.** Real-user QA and accessibility review, the blog post and #HowISwitch post, video edit and voiceover, and Wispr dictation (a second genuine Insights card). Plus registration as a team member and a first-time-user README run on their own machine.
4. **Git.** The teammate is invited as a collaborator on the private repo, works on their own branches through PRs, and does not touch `scripts/gates/`. The repo goes public only after everything is complete and a secret review passes.
5. **Video.** Under 3:00, target 2:15, two real people on camera.
